newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Ailing Portuguese copper firm seeks recovery.
newsitem.headline: Ailing Portuguese copper firm seeks recovery.

text.p: Ailing Portuguese copper company Companhia Portuguesa do Cobre (CPC) may recover under a state initiative to help companies in financial difficulties, its director Figueiroa Goncalves said on Thursday.
"The company lacks cash flow and needs bank credit," Goncalves told Reuters in a telephone interview from the company's headquarters in the northern city of Oporto.
"...we are now looking to the Mateus Plan for a solution, he added."

The so-called Mateus Plan, a recent inititive named after Economy Minister Augusto Mateus, is designed to help ailing companies to recover from their financial problems with the support of bank financing backed by state guarantees.

Some of CPC's 250 workers blocked a road near its factory in Oporto on Wednesday to press the company to pay wage arrears. On Thursday workers lined up at CPC's administrative offices demanding payment, Goncalves said.

CPC, which processes copper, aluminium and brass mainly for domestic industry including state utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, is operating at 25 percent capacity and needs bank credit to pay for raw materials, he said.
CPC's annual turnover had plunged in recent years to around two billion escudos, he added.
